what: UFP Industries makes wood and composite products for three markets: lumber, trusses and wall panels for homebuilders; decking, fencing and lawn products for retailers such as Home Depot; and pallets, crates and packaging for industry.
customers: Homebuilders, home improvement retailers, and industrial companies that ship goods on pallets.
money: Decking, fencing and outdoor products sold through big-box retailers.
Trusses, wall panels and lumber for builders.
moat: Scale in lumber buying and a large network of plants close to customers, which lowers transport costs.
risks: Profits fell every year since 2022 as lumber prices and housing slowed: net income from $693M to $232M over the last twelve months.
Housing starts and home improvement spending are both weak.
Capital spending rose to $269M in 2025, lowering free cash flow.
opportunities: A diversified mix of retail, construction and packaging.
A housing recovery would lift all three segments.
watch: Housing starts, lumber prices and margins in each segment.
view: UFP Industries is a well-run, conservatively financed company at a cyclical low. Profits have fallen every year since the 2022 lumber boom, but the company has net cash and has kept buying back shares.
At about 20 times depressed earnings, the shares are not cheap on today’s profit, but they look reasonable on normal earnings, which have historically been far higher.
This turns on housing. I think it is a good company to own through the cycle, but the timing depends on interest rates and housing recovery, which nobody can predict.
bull: Housing recovers and profits rebound toward previous highs.
bear: Housing stays weak and margins remain under pressure.
